t: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Air National Guard on duty under section 10211, 10305, or 12402 of title 10 or section 708 of title 32, United States Code, or while serving on duty under section 12301(d) of title 10 or section 502(f) of title 32, United States Code, in connection with performing duty specified in section 12310(a) of title 10, United States Code, or while undergoing training, or while performing drills or equivalent duty or other duty, and expenses authorized by section 16131 of title 10, United States Code; and for payments to the Department of Defense Military Retirement Fund, $3,153,990,000.

fable.w: This is an appropriations provision funding pay and related expenses for Air National Guard personnel and payments to the Military Retirement Fund. The mention of the Air National Guard, which has a state connection, could tempt a reading of state coordination, but no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue is involved. No party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Air National Guard

opus.w: This is an appropriations provision that only sets aside funds for Air National Guard personnel costs and payments to the Military Retirement Fund. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. The Guard's ties to the states do not make this participation, because nothing here brings outsiders into a federal decision.
opus.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Air National Guard
opus.b:
1. **Thinking it through.** The one tempting reading is that the Air National Guard is partly a state institution, so this might seem to involve parties outside the federal government. That fails because the section just sets aside money for personnel costs and retirement fund payments. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or allowed to take part in any federal decision.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section is an appropriation for the pay and expenses of Air National Guard personnel while on federal duty. These personnel are considered federal employees in this context, and the provision does not involve consultation with outside parties, public comment, or advisory boards. It is a standard funding authorization for government operations.
qwen_chat.s: For pay, allowances, clothing, subsistence, gratuities, travel, and related expenses for personnel of the Air National Guard on duty under section 10211, 10305, or 12402 of title 10 or section 708 of title 32, United States Code...
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "personnel of the Air National Guard" are outside the federal government because the National Guard is a state militia. However, when they are on federal duty (as specified by the cited titles 10 and 32), they are acting as federal employees. Furthermore, the text is purely an appropriation for their pay and expenses, not a mechanism for them to consult with or influence a federal decision. The definition explicitly excludes applications for benefits or grants, and paying employees is a standard administrative function, not participation.
